subject: ACME order form — proposed output entitlements and productization handshake
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-corp.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme-corp.com, procure@acme-corp.com
Date: Fri, 14 Feb 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACME redlines on MSA + Order Form (v3)

Hi Irene and Redwood team,

Attached are our redlines to the MSA and Order Form (v3). High-level asks:
- Customer wants explicit ownership/attribution for outputs used in customer-facing features; they request a clause that assigns "output title" to Acme where outputs are derived solely from Acme prompts and content.
- Training: we need opt-in language for any model retraining using Acme data; by default Acme data cannot be used to train or improve underlying models without separate written consent.
- Feedback/license: we ask for a perpetual, royalty-free license for feedback that allows Acme to use and sublicense insights generated by Redwood.

Please see the attached doc (ACME_Redlines_MSA_OrderForm_v3.docx) with inline comments. We're aiming to finalize legal language this week so procurement can close PO.

Best,
Jane Doe
General Counsel, Acme Corp
Acme Headquarters

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: sales_ops@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Feb 2025 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: ACME redlines on MSA + Order Form (need legal + product ops guidance)

Forwarding Jane's redlines — tagging legal and product ops. Quick summary of the three pressure points:
1) Output entitlement / "title" ask: ACME wants a carveout that would give them title to outputs in customer-facing products when those outputs are generated entirely from ACME-provided content or prompts. This is broader than our typical order-form language.
2) Training opt-in: they want explicit opt-in for any training use of customer data; default is no training. We have standard language that permits telemetry/avg metrics but not direct model retraining; need clarity on what we can offer.
3) Feedback license: they want a perpetual royalty-free license to use insights/feedback. They likely mean internal/external productization rights.

Questions for legal: what is the minimum language to preserve Redwood's ability to improve models and ship platform-level features while honoring a customer's productization rights? For sales ops: what concessions are acceptable to close without expanding support burden?

I attached a short redlines summary I prepared. Can you propose short, customer-facing compromise options (A = conservative, B = balanced, C = customer-favoring) we can present back to Jane?

Thanks — Irene
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlines_summary.pdf (2 pages)

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 Feb 2025 08:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: ACME redlines on MSA + Order Form (need legal + product ops guidance)

Irene — thanks for the summary. I reviewed ACME's redlines and drafted suggested positions below. I pulled out language that we can present as a narrow compromise; I also flagged non-starters.

Summary of proposed language and rationale:
- Output title: propose "Customer Output Use" clause — Customer has ownership over Outputs strictly to the extent they are (a) derived solely from Customer Inputs and (b) are not materially influenced by Redwood-provided proprietary prompts, templates, or additional training. This preserves Redwood's IP when we supply product-level prompts or tuned components.

Suggested clause (balanced):
"Customer Ownership of Outputs. To the extent any Output is created solely from Customer Inputs and does not incorporate or derive from Redwood proprietary models, prompts, or Customer Data from other customers, Customer shall have the right to use and exploit such Output, including in customer-facing products. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood retains all rights in the underlying models, model weights, and platform technology."

- Training: propose explicit opt-in. Add an Order Form checkbox: "Customer elects to permit Redwood to use Customer Inputs and Outputs to improve Redwood models." Default = unchecked. For customers that opt-in, include data handling/retention safeguards and a 30-day notice for scheduled retraining.

Suggested training clause (short):
"Model Improvement. Redwood will not use Customer Inputs or Outputs to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve Redwood models unless Customer has affirmatively elected such use in the Order Form or an executed amendment. For Customers who elect in, Redwood will apply data minimization, hashing/aggregation, and appropriate retention limits as described in our Data Processing Addendum."

- Feedback/license: limit scope to a non-exclusive license for Redwood to use feedback internally and limited external uses for as-delivered feature improvements; do not grant perpetual sublicensable rights to Customer over Redwood IP. If ACME wants to surface insights externally, that should be scoped to their Outputs (per the Output clause).

Suggested feedback language:
"Feedback License. Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use feedback provided by Customer to improve Redwood products and services. Such license does not transfer any title to Redwood intellectual property. Customer may use Outputs consistent with the Customer Ownership of Outputs clause but does not receive rights to Redwood model weights or proprietary prompts."

Action items / options to present to ACME:
A) Conservative: Accept training opt-in only; decline output title (offer broad usage rights but not title).
B) Balanced (recommended): Accept Output ownership for strictly defined Outputs (customer-only inputs), explicit opt-in for training via Order Form, limited internal feedback license for Redwood.
C) Customer-favoring: Grant broader output title and a perpetual feedback license — only for enterprise with material commercial commitment (higher fees + dedicated support + explicit indemnities).

I can draft redline text to insert into their doc. Connor/Markus — please confirm operational impact for option B (billing, support SLAs, tagging ingested data) so we can quantify commercial equivalence.

- Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-corp.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, procure@acme-corp.com
Date: Sun, 16 Feb 2025 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: ACME redlines on MSA + Order Form — proposed compromise (draft)

Hi Jane — thanks for the detailed redlines and the quick turnaround. We've reviewed internally and propose a balanced path forward that should protect ACME's ability to productize outputs derived from your proprietary inputs while preserving Redwood's ability to operate and improve the inference platform.

Key points we'll propose (high level):
- Output ownership: we can grant usage and exploitation rights for Outputs created solely from ACME Inputs (we propose the wording Laura suggested). We cannot assign title to Redwood's models, prompts, or model weights.
- Training: we will require explicit opt-in on the Order Form for any use of ACME Inputs/Outputs to retrain or fine-tune Redwood models. Default will be no training. If ACME opts in, we'll include additional safeguards (aggregation, retention limits).
- Feedback license: Redwood needs a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use feedback for product improvements; if ACME needs broader rights to the platform IP or perpetual sublicensable rights, that would require an enterprise amendment and commercial terms.

Operational ask: Connor/Markus will confirm if any tagging/ingestion overhead for opt-in customers will require a change order or uplift in fees. Laura — attached is a draft redline with our recommended inserts.

If this approach sounds reasonable I can send a short note with proposed clauses and a redline back to your legal team this week. If ACME prefers the broader customer-favoring option we will need to move to a commercial amendment (higher fee + dedicated eng support) — happy to discuss.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
